first_words: It does not roar. It breathes, long and slow, and the sound fills the dark.
It comes out of the dark without hurry, as if this is the hundredth time and you are the hundredth hunter.
A sound like a mill-wheel turning, somewhere in the dark ahead. Then it comes.
It lowers itself, and gathers, and looks at you with something like hate.
It shakes itself, and old blood flies from it, and it opens its jaws wide.
It smells you before it sees you, and it is glad.
omens: A dead raven on the path, its head bitten clean away.
Every dog in the hamlet you pass is howling, and none of them will say why.
The birds go quiet in the trees around you, all at once, as if a door had shut.
The brambles torn and wet at the height of your shoulder, as if something big had pushed through.
A shepherd's crook broken in two and thrown down in the road.
Somewhere far off, on the wind, a sound that might be a laugh and is certainly not.
The horses will not settle. They stare at the treeline with their ears flat.
A trail of blood crossing the road, still wet, going nowhere you can see.

first_words: "You have come," it says, as if it had sent for you. "Good. Kneel, and it will be quicker."
"Everything that is happening was promised long ago," it says. "You are only the last line of the prophecy."
"I do not hate you," it says. "The fire does not hate the field. It only burns."
It lifts both hands, and its voice fills the place like a bell. "Witness!"
"There is still time to be saved," it says, and it means it, and that is the worst of it.
"You are an offering," it says gently. "You were always going to be an offering."
omens: A shrine by the road has been broken open, and its saint's face scratched out.
Someone has painted a sign in red on the milestone, an eye with no lid.
The bells of a chapel far off ring the hour wrong, and then fall silent.
A crowd of birds circles over the hills, always the same way round, and none of them lands.
A dead goat hangs from a roadside tree, its throat cut neatly and its blood caught in a bowl.
A beggar at the crossroads looks up as you pass and says your name, and then forgets he said it.
Candles burn in a ruined chapel at noon, and nobody is inside.
A child is singing a hymn you have never heard, and stops when you look at her.

fizzle: What {name} was gathering breaks apart and is gone.
{name} loses hold of it: the gathered force spills away to nothing.
Whatever {name} was making ready dies before it can be loosed.
The moment passes. {name} cannot finish what it began.

entrance: Out of the dark of its den {name} comes, and the ground takes its weight with a sound like a dropped sack of stones.
{name} lifts its head from what it was eating, and the light finds its eyes, and it comes.
Something huge unfolds from the shadows at the back of the den. {name} is awake, and you are in its home.

great.name: the rampage
warn: {name} drops low and gathers itself, every muscle bunching. Whatever is near it when it moves will be under it.
{name} goes still and coils, head down, tail lashing. It is about to throw its whole weight round.
A long rumble comes out of {name}, and it braces its feet wide. Get clear of it.
go: {name} explodes into motion, whirling through everything round it.
{name} lunges and spins, and the ground round it is a storm of claws and bulk.
{name} throws itself round in a great sweep, smashing at everything in reach.

lines: Cornered and bleeding, it stops being careful.
It howls, and when it comes again it comes like a landslide.
Something breaks in it. It is past fear now, and past cunning.
It has had enough of you, for now. It turns and goes, faster than anything that size should move.
Bleeding, it backs off a step, and another, and then it is gone into the dark towards its den.
It gives one long look at you, as if to remember your faces, and runs.

troll.name: fire
lore: The old ones say {villain_short} hates fire more than it hates the hunters: its wounds that are burned do not close.
Fire. The tales all agree on it. Whatever {villain_short} is, burning flesh stays burned.
"Bring fire," the old songs say of beasts like this one. "Iron cuts, but fire ends."

lore: The old ones say {villain_short} hates fire more than it hates the hunters: its wounds that are burned do not close.

ogre.name: its greed
lore: It is greedy, the tales say. It has never once passed by a meal laid out for it, though it knew it was a trap.
Its hunger is its weakness: lay out meat and it will come to it, every time, and come blind.
Old hunters of {area} say it is bait that kills such beasts, not blades: it cannot help itself.

dire_wolf.name: fire in the hand
lore: Fire frightens it, as it frightens every beast: a burning brand thrust in its face will make it shy.
It is a beast still, for all its name: fire in the hand will turn it, for a moment.
The hunters' trick is old and simple: a torch in the face, and it falters long enough for a blow.

tokens: a page torn from a journal
a comb with a few hairs still in it
missing: Later, {token_of} goes looking for {token}, and cannot find it anywhere.
Somewhere on the way {token_of} has lost {token}, or thinks so. Nobody saw anyone come near.
{token_of} turns the pack out twice that evening. {token} is gone, and nobody can say where.
It is only {token}, and {token_of} laughs about losing it. Nobody else laughs.

offers: a pardon for an old crime, and the name cleared
enough gold to buy a farm and never be found
the life of a brother who is dying
word of the child they lost, and where she is now
a place at its side when the country is its own
a cure for the sickness that runs in their blood
